Only two criteria conflict with a siting decision in any area of the county: locations of wetlands and open water, and slope. Given the greater tolerance for slope, this obstruction is minimal. Finally we look to the propensity for collocation in Rosebud County, which is shown in Table M.R5. Due to the lack of meaningful siting restrictions for data centers, collocation is almost exclusively dependent upon the potential for siting the various reactor technologies discussed in this body of work. Accordingly, the potential for collocation for both the large water reactor and stream-cooled SMR technologies lies predominantly around the Yellowstone River, which increases to most of the northern portion of the county for the dry-cooled SMR.
